manifest.title: AWS DMS: Aurora PostgreSQL to TiDB
manifest.tagline: Full load, live CDC, and a measured cutover from Aurora PostgreSQL to TiDB using AWS DMS.
manifest.pattern: Fintech evaluating a move from Aurora PostgreSQL to TiDB, testing AWS DMS full load plus CDC as the migration path.

metrics.label: Full load throughput
metrics.howMeasured: Delta of FullLoadRows from DescribeTableStatistics between ticks, divided by tick interval seconds.

metrics.label: Full load completion
metrics.howMeasured: FullLoadRows / sourceRowCount * 100 per table, sourceRowCount taken once via SELECT COUNT(*) on Aurora PostgreSQL at phase start.

metrics.label: CDC latency (source)
metrics.howMeasured: CloudWatch metric CDCLatencySource (namespace AWS/DMS), most recent datapoint per tick via GetMetricData.

metrics.label: CDC latency (target)
metrics.howMeasured: CloudWatch metric CDCLatencyTarget (namespace AWS/DMS), most recent datapoint per tick via GetMetricData.

metrics.label: CDC apply throughput
metrics.howMeasured: Delta of AppliedInserts + AppliedUpdates + AppliedDeletes from DescribeTableStatistics between ticks, divided by tick interval seconds.

metrics.label: Validation failures
metrics.howMeasured: ValidationFailedRecords from DescribeTableStatistics, summed across tables.

metrics.label: Row count difference
metrics.howMeasured: ABS(pg_count - tidb_count) from the runner's own SELECT COUNT(*) on both databases.

metrics.label: End-to-end freshness
metrics.howMeasured: visibleAt - insertedAt for a timestamped heartbeat row inserted into Aurora PostgreSQL and polled for on TiDB.

metrics.label: Cutover downtime
metrics.howMeasured: Wall-clock seconds from stopping the load generator to confirming a successful write against the new TiDB connection.

phases.label: Provision and verify
phases.narration: Aurora PostgreSQL, AWS DMS, and TiDB Cloud are up. This is the same DMS you already use for other migrations.

phases.label: Schema conversion
phases.narration: DMS creates tables and primary keys. Everything else in the type conversion is explicit, and we show you exactly what changed.

phases.label: Full load
phases.narration: DMS full-loads the existing orders and accounts tables while the app keeps taking traffic.

phases.label: CDC under live load
phases.narration: Now every insert, update, and delete on Aurora flows through logical replication into TiDB, live.

phases.label: Validate
phases.narration: We don't just trust DMS's validation state, we recompute row counts and checksums ourselves on both databases.

phases.label: Cutover
phases.narration: Writes stop, CDC drains to zero lag, we verify one more time, then the app points at TiDB. That whole window is the downtime we measure.

checks.label: Schema parity
checks.description: Every TiDB column has a documented source PostgreSQL type in the plan's mapping table.

checks.label: Row count match
checks.description: SELECT COUNT(*) is equal on Aurora PostgreSQL and TiDB for every migrated table.

checks.label: Checksum match
checks.description: A per-table checksum aggregate is equal on both sides.

checks.label: Clean cutover
checks.description: CDCLatencyTarget is 0 and both row-count-match and checksum-match pass immediately before the connection flip.

controls.label: Burst writes
controls.description: Raise the load generator's write rate against Aurora PostgreSQL for 30 seconds.

controls.label: Run validation
controls.description: Compute row counts and checksums on both databases and emit check events.

controls.label: Start cutover
controls.description: Stop the load generator, drain CDC latency to zero, re-validate, then flip the app's connection to TiDB.

events.observed: TiDB DDL documented against PostgreSQL source types (infra/sql/schema.sql, schema-tidb.sql)
